problem: Floor plan-guided navigation has only been studied for PointNav in a few small environments (e.g. FloNa), so whether floor plans help ObjectNav and ImageNav, and how to build one model for all goal types, is unexplored. Existing mapping-based or mapless methods either spend effort exploring or lack global guidance.
motivation: Floor plans are cheap, temporally stable and encode geometry plus implicit semantics (room function, typical object placement), so they can serve as spatial priors for inferring goal locations in unseen scenes. A large-scale benchmark and a unified policy are needed to test this across goal modalities.
key_idea: Unify point, object and image goal navigation in one floor-plan-conditioned two-stage diffusion policy: a masked-modality goal planner produces a coarse trajectory, and a depth/SDF-based refiner makes it collision-safe.
insight: Removing the floor plan lowers SR by 16.2/6.3/7.7 points on PointNav/ImageNav/ObjectNav, and the qualitative comparison shows trajectories head more directly toward the goal with the plan, so the plan gives usable priors even for semantic goals, with the largest gain on PointNav where geometry is explicit. Joint training with random modality masking improves ImageNav (28.9 vs 25.4) and ObjectNav (28.6 vs 24.3) over single-modality models, while PointNav stays about the same, suggesting geometric knowledge from PointNav transfers to semantic goals. The refiner ablation shows the depth-derived SDF matters most for PointNav (SR 34.3 to 42.0).
method: FloVerse task/dataset: a floor plan (one level per plan) plus egocentric RGBD and pose; goal is a point, object category or goal image. 1,627 floor plans (1,488 HM3D, 139 Gibson 4+) are extracted automatically by slicing the mesh at 1.25 m above floor height, followed by morphological denoising. About 240K A* expert trajectories (waypoints every 10 cm) and 12M RGBD-pose pairs. Object goals cover 325 categories across 299 scenes, built from HM3D-OVON plus SpatialLM detections with manual filtering.

Multi-modality goal-conditioned planner: at each training iteration only one of three goal conditions is kept (random modality masking). Point goal uses an MLP; image goal uses EfficientNet features of the current RGB and goal image; object goal uses frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 features of the current image and the label. Observation features are self-attention over the past l steps of RGB, depth and pose. Floor plan features come from EfficientNet-B0.

Diffusion trajectory generator: conditional U-Net with a DDPM scheduler, conditioned on goal, floor plan and observation features, predicts 16 future waypoints (of which the first 10 are executed) with an MSE noise-prediction loss.

Depth-based trajectory refiner: depth is projected to a 20x50 local BEV occupancy map at 0.1 m, converted to an SDF, and encoded by a CNN. A second diffusion model takes the coarse trajectory plus the SDF embedding and outputs a refined trajectory. Loss = MSE + 0.1 * mean exp(-rho_i) collision loss, with rho_i the SDF distance interpolated for differentiability.

Training and inference: stage 1 is trained to convergence, then both stages are trained jointly (AdamW, lr 1e-4, up to 20 epochs, 4x4090, batch 32/GPU). Inference averages 30 sampled trajectories per step and uses a collision-rollback safety mechanism; runtime is 0.18 s/step.

setting.backbone: Two conditional U-Net DDPM diffusion models with EfficientNet-B0 encoders (trained from scratch) and frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 for object goals
setting.training_data: FloVerse expert trajectories: ~240K trajectories (198,150 HM3D + 18,150 Gibson 4+ train episodes; 1,321 + 121 scenes), 12M RGBD-pose pairs; ImageNav/ObjectNav on 65,700 HM3D episodes
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + 2D pose history + 2D floor plan image
setting.action_space: predicted 2D waypoint trajectory (16 waypoints, first 10 executed), converted to global positions/orientations
setting.simulator: Gibson simulator (Habitat-based); HM3D and Gibson 4+ scenes
setting.privileged: Floor plan of the test scene (derived from GT mesh) and agent pose/odometry at test time; goal image or GT point goal

numbers_note: Custom FloVerse benchmark (own split, not an official benchmark). The PointNav SPL for the full model is 36.6 in Table w/o F and 36.4 in the refiner table (a small inconsistency). Refiner ablation: w/o refiner PointNav SR 34.3/SPL 29.2, ImageNav 27.7/21.4, ObjectNav 25.3/19.4. GOAT-Bench numbers are split into ImageNav and ObjectNav subtasks.
results: FloVerse beats FloDiff fine-tuned on PointNav (Gibson 4+ SR 54.4 vs 38.8; HM3D 38.1 vs 27.7) and fine-tuned Nomad on ImageNav (28.9 vs 22.8 SR), and far exceeds ZSON on ObjectNav. On GOAT-Bench val-seen it beats Modular GOAT in ObjectNav (SR 34.5 vs 29.4, SPL 30.8 vs 17.0) and gets the best SPL in ImageNav (25.6), though RL Skill Chain has higher ImageNav SR (42.2).
limitations: Only residential indoor floor plans; other building types are untested.
Floor plans are auto-generated from GT meshes rather than real plans, and there is no real-robot evaluation.
Absolute success rates are low (ImageNav and ObjectNav below 30% on FloVerse), and ImageNav/ObjectNav gains from floor plans are modest.
compares_to: GOAT-Bench baselines (RL Monolithic, RL Skill Chain, Modular GOAT)
